children.translated_text: Seated comfortably in his hermitage,
learned in the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>śāstras</s>,
[contd.]
the sages approached and asked
<s>Yama</s>, whose mind was controlled.
[contd.]
'Those who are tainted by great sins
and likewise by minor sins,
[contd.]
by which observances are they purified?
Tell us that, O great sage.'
[contd.]
'Water touched by wind and sun during the day,
by the stars and wind at night,
[contd.]
and by both twilights at the two junctures —
water is always pure.
[contd.]
That which is naturally present, not permeated
by impure substances, is always clean;
[contd.]
drinking water, whether stored in a vessel or on the ground,
is purifying for men.
[contd.]
But a <s>dvija</s> (twice-born) who has been touched by an impure substance,
whether at night or during the day,
[contd.]
should immediately bathe and touch fire,
and at the two twilights he is always pure.
[contd.]
Bitten by wild beasts, camels, horses, and the like,
but not by humans —
[contd.]
a man becomes pure immediately upon bathing
at the twilights and at night.
[contd.]
One who unknowingly eats food from
a <s>caṇḍāla</s> (outcaste) in any manner,
[contd.]
subsisting on cow's urine and barley gruel,
is purified in ten nights.
[contd.]
Those who have fallen by water, fire, hanging,
who have fallen from renunciation, fasting, or from a vow,
[contd.]
who have attempted suicide by poison or falling,
and those struck and killed by weapons —
[contd.]
these nine are called fallen persons,
excluded from all religious rites.
[contd.]
They are purified by <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> (lunar penance)
or by two <s>taptakṛcchra</s> (heated penances).
[contd.]
Sinners who dwell in both (extremes),
who have fallen from the dark-spotted (impure) condition,
[contd.]
are purified by two lunar penances,
having given a cow and a bull.
[contd.]
Having cremated a cow or <s>brāhmaṇa</s> killed by another,
or one dead by hanging,
[contd.]
and having cut the ropes of that person,
one should perform the <s>sāṃtapana kṛcchra</s> (heated penance).
[contd.]
One afflicted by worms born from a wound,
or harmed by flies and such insects —
[contd.]
should perform <s>kṛcchra</s> for a year,
<s>parāka</s> (penance), due to contact with delusion.
[contd.]
For each individual sin committed,
the wise know the appropriate penance;
[contd.]
but for the accumulation of all sins,
there is no penance.
[contd.]
For the accumulation of all sins,
carrying a skull is prescribed;
[contd.]
that <s>kāpālika</s> (skull-bearing) is the foremost
penance, according to the wise.
[contd.]
For those who eat the food of <s>kāpālikas</s>,
and likewise for those who consort with their women,
[contd.]
if done knowingly, <s>kṛcchra</s> for a year is prescribed;
if unknowingly, two lunar penances.
[contd.]
For drinking <s>surā</s> (liquor) or other intoxicants,
or even for eating cow's flesh,
[contd.]
one afflicted by <s>taptakṛcchra</s> (heated penance)
is purified by a <s>mauñjīhoma</s> (fire offering with muñja grass).
[contd.]
If the performer dies while the penance
is not yet completed,
[contd.]
he is purified on that very day
in this world and the next.
[contd.]
As long as a person performs a penance
without separate possessions,
[contd.]
those unpraiseworthy persons who touch him
shall become censured.
[contd.]
They are not to be dined with, not to receive gifts from,
not to be studied with, not to be married —
[contd.]
but when his vow is fulfilled, they are purified,
[contd.]
[contd.]
[contd.]
who share in the inheritance.
all of them
[contd.]
One who is eighty years old,
or a child under sixteen,
[contd.]
deserves half the penance,
as do women and the sick.
[contd.]
For one who has not yet completed sixteen years
or is over four years of age,
[contd.]
a brother, or a father, or another kinsman
should perform the penance.
[contd.]
For one younger than that,
there is neither fault nor sin;
[contd.]
there is no royal punishment for him,
nor is penance prescribed.
[contd.]
One should perform the <s>sāṃtapana kṛcchra</s>
for killing a person of mixed birth;
[contd.]
for killing a <s>sūta</s> (charioteer caste), the <s>atikṛcchra</s> penance,
and likewise for a <s>kuṇḍa</s> or <s>golaka</s> (illegitimate offspring).
[contd.]
For killing women without distinction,
one should perform the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> (lunar penance) vow;
[contd.]
for killing a cow, a <s>kṣatriya</s>, a <s>vaiśya</s>,
a <s>śūdra</s>, or one born in the regular order.
[contd.]
For eating their food, consorting with their women,
and likewise for accepting gifts from them,
[contd.]
one should properly perform <s>kṛcchra</s> for a year or year-long <s>kṛcchra</s>
for the sake of purification.
[contd.]
One who causes the destruction of another living being
should give a gift according to his ability;
[contd.]
he should also always perform <s>kṛcchra</s> —
the <s>prājāpatya</s> penance is the established rule.
[contd.]
The four perpetrators of great sins,
without distinction,
[contd.]
are purified by entering fire
or by bathing at a horse sacrifice.
[contd.]
But those who commit sins in secret,
in the month of <s>Māgha</s>, with manly effort,
[contd.]
reciting the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s> hymn,
are purified while standing in water.
[contd.]
For intercourse with another's wife, with a man, with a eunuch,
with horses, goats, sheep, or cattle —
[contd.]
up to intercourse with a cow, one should practice the
<s>Pāvamānī</s> verses and chant for three days.
[contd.]
Those who have sexual intercourse with women
of the <s>caṇḍāla</s> and other outcaste groups, or with cows,
[contd.]
are purified by reciting the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s> for a fortnight
while observing a milk diet.
[contd.]
One who has relations with his mother, his teacher's wife,
his sister, or his daughter —
[contd.]
should enter fire;
no other purification is prescribed.
[contd.]
One who has relations with the sister of his father or mother,
the daughter of his own son, or the wife of a maternal uncle,
[contd.]
or the wife of his son —
should perform <s>kṛcchra</s> for six months.
[contd.]
The six and four other women
who are relatives on the father's and mother's side —
[contd.]
for having relations with these and with a woman of the same <s>gotra</s> (lineage),
one should perform the <s>parāka</s> <s>kṛcchra</s> penance.
[contd.]
A washerman, a leatherworker,
an actor, a <s>buruḍa</s> (basket-maker),
[contd.]
a fisherman, a performer,
a wrestler — these are outcastes.
[contd.]
For eating or drinking with these,
or for secretly consorting with them even once,
[contd.]
or for having oral intercourse,
one should perform the <s>taptakṛcchra</s> (heated penance).
[contd.]
<s>Caṇḍālas</s>, <s>muṣṭikas</s> (boxers),
and likewise those born of mixed unions —
[contd.]
for eating their food, consorting with their women,
and likewise for accepting gifts from them,
[contd.]
if done knowingly, <s>kṛcchra</s> for a year is prescribed;
if unknowingly, the lunar penance is prescribed.
[contd.]
Those for whom the family tradition prescribes
liquor-drinking for women,
[contd.]
and those born in fallen lineages —
they are known as followers of improper family customs.
[contd.]
Those of all four <s>varṇas</s> (social classes)
who are outside yet consider themselves <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,
[contd.]
mixed through generations —
they should be carefully avoided.
[contd.]
One born from a fallen and degraded man
and a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> woman, or from a <s>śūdra</s> —
[contd.]
both of those should be known as <s>caṇḍālas</s>,
as is one born from a man of the same <s>gotra</s>.
[contd.]
One born of adultery from a woman of the same <s>varṇa</s>
is called a <s>kuṇḍa</s> while the husband lives;
[contd.]
when the husband is dead, he is called a <s>golaka</s> —
both of them are likewise deprived of caste.
[contd.]
And those begotten by <s>dvijas</s> (twice-born)
upon women of different <s>varṇas</s>,
[contd.]
and upon all other men's wives —
they are known as <s>kuṇḍas</s> and <s>golakas</s>.
[contd.]
They are not said to belong to the mother's <s>varṇa</s>,
nor are they considered of the father's <s>varṇa</s>;
[contd.]
their children are not to be married
by relatives on either the father's or mother's side.
[contd.]
By those dependent on the mother, by those associated with the king,
by the very young or very old, and by those oppressed by the king —
[contd.]
speech uttered by these is not authoritative evidence;

children.text: na hy uttaraṃ naiva kṛtaṃ kṛtās te
children.translated_text: neither a reply nor a deed — such persons are disqualified.
[contd.]
The killer of a horse, the killer of a man,
the cutter of trees nourished by pots (i.e. cultivated),
[contd.]
and those who are addicted to another's wife —
they deserve death by weapons, not a lighter punishment.
[contd.]
He who with evil intent kills another,
who harms a wife, a son, a spouse,
[contd.]
a field, grain, wealth, or body —
him the king should kill with blows of a mace.
[contd.]
The doer, the consenter, the giver of advice,
the instigator, and the one who retaliates,
[contd.]
the counselor, the helper, the one who dwells with the condemned —
the clearing of suspicion should be done by a man.
[contd.]
He who is attached as a dependent, servant, or food-recipient of another —
when a fault is committed by that man, the master is the doer;
[contd.]
but when it is directed at the one who enjoys the offering, there is no liability;
the giver of food is released.
[contd.]
Others upon others, struck by greed,
and the high and low, and others upon others.
[contd.]
At sacrifices, weddings, and festivals,
whether among those of the same husband or different husbands,
[contd.]
the annual activity of cooking for others —
in these cases, they say there is no fault in giving food.
[contd.]
Even a giver of weapons or poison and fire,
having given them to another, completes a month (of penance);
[contd.]
if for the purpose of obtaining <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, or <s>kāma</s>,
and if the activity does not harm another.
[contd.]

children.text: yo vāhanaṃ kartari vāraṇaṃ vā hy
children.translated_text: He who takes a vehicle or an elephant of the perpetrator
and goes away with undiscriminating mind —
[contd.]
even therein, experts declare no fault;
he is pure in that matter, yet punishable in the same way.
[contd.]
A wife, a son, a daughter-in-law, a daughter's child,
a brother, a son, a hired servant, or a dependent —
[contd.]
whoever is guilty of a fault should be punished by the king;
but the non-doer who is the master — this is the <s>dharma</s>.
[contd.]
By the giving of wealth, equally or unequally,
by the application of action, and likewise by battle —
[contd.]
he who dwells in the mind of a man
is to be known as a companion in happiness and sorrow.
[contd.]
Whether a large animal, a bird, a beast, a domestic animal,
of the same species or of another —
[contd.]
if unprovoked it kills a man or a woman,
the owner's sacrificial cows should not be seized.
[contd.]
Whatever caste belongs to the <s>dvija</s> class —
for sacrifices and such, sinners should not be punished;
[contd.]
those confined and bound in the giving of planets (astrological affairs) —
serpents do not harm those who are fearless of others.
[contd.]
Having made the wealthy man pay for that (damage),
the owner should be released with the price of the animal.
[contd.]
In disputes about <s>dharma</s>, if cows and such
die by their own will or by accident,
[contd.]
even therein, the knowers of <s>dharma</s> do not declare
either fault or the measure of the animal (as compensation).
[contd.]
If wild cattle or those with tusks
die, and if they are uncremated —
[contd.]
in restraining sinners, they do not declare it as sin
for the one who gives the noose with his own hand.
[contd.]
When one person is killed by many together,
and it is not known by whose blows the death occurred,
[contd.]
the killer should be ascertained by ordeal,
and apprehended by those appointed by the king.
[contd.]
One who has abandoned life sometimes dies
sinlessly, through the act of purification from sin.
[contd.]
Some say, having reasoned by means of logic and evidence,
'This is the authoritative teaching' —
[contd.]
'The eternally-inmost living being never dies' —

children.text: vedaiś ca pṛṣṭair ṛṣibhiś ca gītaṃ
children.translated_text: this is declared by the <s>Vedas</s> and sung by the sages.
[contd.]
<s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s> and other purifying rites —
when sinners wish to perform them for their benefit,
[contd.]
and they wish for association, the fruit would be thus:
by the lamp of knowledge, in the darkness of ignorance.
[contd.]
Those men who, having arrived at the state
requiring penance, do not perform their vows —
[contd.]
hear the punishment and vow prescribed
for them in order.
[contd.]
But he who, having himself confessed his sin,
performs the penance —
[contd.]
punishment should not be applied to him;
the vow itself is accepted as the punishment.
[contd.]
In a major sin, there is no monetary punishment;
in an equal fault, there is punishment.
[contd.]
One who does not perform the vow therein
should be made to pay a fine of one thousand.
[contd.]
A man who is guilty of a minor sin
and does not perform the vow —
[contd.]
always first should come the non-violent
purificatory penance.
[contd.]
For killing a blue jay, a frog, a cat,
a cow-lizard, an owl, and crows,
[contd.]
a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> incurs a fine of one hundred;
and indeed for a mongoose.
[contd.]
For peacocks, geese, and herons,
and likewise hawks and roosters —
[contd.]
one incurs a fine of thirty <s>paṇas</s>;
and likewise for a wild peacock.
[contd.]
A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who has abandoned the sacred fire,
who neglects the twilight worship,
[contd.]
and who serves a <s>śūdra</s> —
the king should banish him from the realm.
[contd.]
A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who has abandoned the sacred fire,
who does not bathe or recite <s>mantras</s>,
[contd.]
who does not worship or attend to the Sun,
a <s>dvija</s> who does not observe the twilight worship,
[contd.]
who does not perform the daily sacrifices,
who eats the food of a <s>śūdra</s> —
[contd.]
even while living, by these transgressions,
he should incur a fine of one <s>paṇa</s> daily.
[contd.]
A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who deposits his seed in <s>śūdra</s> women,
or who desires a low-caste woman —
[contd.]
having confiscated all his property,
should be branded on the forehead with the mark of a vulva.
[contd.]
The vulva-mark, the liquor-mark,
the <s>surā</s>-mark on the forehead,
[contd.]
for one who deposits his seed in prostitutes —
the king should confiscate everything.
[contd.]
One who does not bathe properly, who bathes during the day (at improper times),
who eats another's food as well as his own,
[contd.]
who eats though his rituals are destroyed —
they declare his property forfeit to the king.
[contd.]
The property declared abandoned by the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>,
of one who habitually eats <s>śūdra</s> food —
[contd.]
every year, confiscating everything,
one should offer it to those learned in the <s>Vedas</s>.
[contd.]
Wearing the upper garment improperly,
or committing violence through unjust punishment —
[contd.]
one who does so to a woman
should be made to pay double the fine.
[contd.]
For children, the blind, the sick, and the aged,
no punishment is prescribed.
[contd.]
A man who urinates
on a highway and such places incurs a fault.
[contd.]
Likewise regarding defecation,
and vomiting should not occur on the road;
[contd.]
double the punishment is incurred
by one who stands while urinating.
[contd.]
One who urinates facing
the eastern (<s>Māhendra</s>) or western (<s>Vāruṇa</s>) direction,
[contd.]
and likewise one who defecates thus —
incurs double the punishment.
[contd.]
A thief, a slanderer,
a violent man, the husband of a <s>śūdra</s> woman —
[contd.]
these should be known as the abandoned and unrestrained,
five thorns of the village.
[contd.]
Having identified and released these thorns
throughout his realms, the king —
[contd.]
for if not released, they cause
falsehood and darkness in the world.
[contd.]
Smeared with excrement and such filth,
adorned with garlands of blood-flowers,
[contd.]
having been nourished by thieving activities —
the king should execute the thief.
[contd.]
Placing a dog's jaw in the slanderer's mouth,
wrapping him in a donkey's skin,
[contd.]
mounting the slanderer on a donkey,
having confiscated his wealth, the king should banish him.
[contd.]
Having broken into houses, stolen property,
and even prepared instruments for that purpose —
[contd.]
the king should expel the violent criminal from the realm,
casting him out like a <s>caṇḍāla</s>.
[contd.]
Breaking his vow, a liquor vessel —
both of these are then bound to him;
[contd.]
his heart smeared with excrement,
the king should banish the husband of a <s>śūdra</s> woman.
[contd.]
His body also smeared with ashes,
perfumed with the hair and bones of a corpse,
[contd.]
having confiscated everything from the one who has abandoned the sacred fire,
the king should banish him from the realm.
[contd.]
Being fanned with the hair of a corpse,
with a garland of those hairs bound on his head,
[contd.]
the king should send naked throughout the land
the man who violates a convention.
[contd.]
A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of the lowest kind who has produced offspring
in <s>śūdra</s> women, having royal associations —
[contd.]
the king should place him outside the village,
a man guilty of the sin of association.
[contd.]
One who deposits his seed in such a woman,
having mixed him among virtuous people,
[contd.]
and having him eat in the same row —
he should receive the first (degree of) punishment.
[contd.]
Wealth given, and likewise what is wrongfully acquired,
and what is studied by <s>dvijas</s> and others —
[contd.]
all becomes fruitless
through the speech of slanderous men.
[contd.]
One who reveals weaknesses to a thief
regarding the property of gods, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, or kinswomen —
[contd.]
such a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> incurs physical punishment
for having taken all the wealth.
[contd.]
The one who reveals weaknesses to thieves
is himself called a thief;
[contd.]
having confiscated all his property,
a dog's paw should be branded upon his face.
[contd.]
One born at night — at night indeed
a man is known by his marks;
[contd.]
and likewise, having recognized a false speaker
by his marks, the king should banish him.
[contd.]
A false speaker in a dispute
the king, having punished the witness,
who conceals the sins of the wicked,
should prescribe a penance of twenty days.
One performing the observance of <s>vrata</s> (penance), living on alms,
and not having offered oblations to the fire,
may eat and obtain a morsel of food
at the proper times, if not afflicted by illness.
Of the teacher, the father, the brother,
the father-in-law, and the king,
a man who does not rise to greet them
shall be made to pay a fine of three <s>paṇas</s>.
But when seated on the same seat,
and a superior is standing nearby,
a <s>Śūdra</s> incurs a fine of six <s>paṇas</s>;
and one who departs without rising when the other is leaving,
Measures of weight and capacity,
whether greater or lesser, in a dispute over speech,
in whose possession they are found, his property
shall be assigned to the king — so it is ordained.
Sesame oil mixed
and sold under the name of ghee,
the merchant shall be made to pay fourfold;
or oil mixed with ghee likewise.
Pepper adulterated with stone fragments,
and salt likewise with earth,
and <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida) with tree resins —
likewise he shall be made to pay fourfold.
Grain mixed with chaff and stones,
or indeed adulterated again,
the seller shall be made to pay an equal amount,
and shall give to that buyer the adulterated goods as well.
With equal or unequal substances,
having adulterated goods and then selling to people,
a fourfold fine is prescribed;
by this rule one should always conduct oneself.
Sweepings from a funeral, filth,
broken pots, and husks,
one who casts them on the road of the village
one <s>paṇa</s>.
shall be made to pay
Leftover water and drippings,
a householder who discharges them on the road,
incurs a double fine;
one who releases urine shall be fined one <s>rūpya</s> (silver coin).
Having killed a rooster by day,
a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> shall pay three <s>paṇas</s>;
for killing a hare, a tortoise, an iguana,
or a ram — sixteen <s>paṇas</s>.
Milk, milk products,
salt, and oil,
and lac — a <s>Vipra</s> (brahmin) who engages in selling these
incurs the middling fine.
Cakes, cooked food, meat,
<s>Soma</s>, bones, and honey,
and bark — one who engages in selling these
shall incur the middling fine.
The superintendent of the father's affairs,
cheating in unequal measure,
incurs a fine of one <s>paṇa</s>;
and the consumer also, in the case of unequal measure.
A <s>Vipra</s> (brahmin) who has begotten offspring
with a <s>Vṛṣalī</s> (śūdra woman) and then marries her,
incurs a fine of one thousand;
this applies when the first offspring has been born.
A <s>Vipra</s> (brahmin) who eats the cooked food
of a husband of a <s>Vṛṣalī</s> (śūdra woman),
incurs fourteen <s>paṇas</s>;
double that during the period of birth-impurity.
Having eaten a <s>Śrāddha</s> (ancestral rite) meal in that house,
one shall incur the same number of <s>paṇas</s>;
one incurs the first degree of <s>sāhasa</s> (violent crime) penalty,
especially when there is no justification.
One who eats the <s>Anvaṣṭakā</s> or <s>Aṣṭakā</s> meal
at the house of the husband of a <s>Vṛṣalī</s>,
incurs fourteen <s>paṇas</s>;
and likewise one who eats the monthly offering.
Even taking food in sequence from the <s>Aṣṭakā</s> distribution
from the abode of one married to a <s>Vṛṣalā</s>,
one incurs half of ninety-six;
and for having eaten previously in that house.
For consuming liquor and other forbidden foods,
a <s>Vipra</s> (brahmin) incurs sixteen <s>paṇas</s>;
double for crushed or pressed foods;
for fish, one incurs a hundred.
Thus double the penalty shall be given
for these offenses by <s>Soma</s>-drinkers (those initiated into Soma sacrifice);
for eating the flesh of donkeys, horses, pigs, and the like,
one is declared fallen.
With wooden objects, bones, horns, or stones,
a <s>Dvija</s> (twice-born) who strikes his wife,
incurs a fine of one thousand;
and if he shaves her head as well.
On the limbs, in visible places,
one who wounds his wife with nails,
whether doing it himself or having it done, with his own limbs,
shall be made to pay the first degree of fine.
A <s>Dvija</s> (twice-born) who eats from a woman's mouth,
or who drinks water from a well,
and likewise one who feeds his own wife thus,
shall be made to pay the first <s>sāhasa</s> penalty.
And one who excessively proclaims it,
such a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> becomes fallen;
one who approaches a woman in the manner of a horse,
or kisses the private parts,
a <s>Vipra</s> (brahmin) who deliberately emits semen
shall incur fifty <s>paṇas</s>;
for having intercourse with cows,
he shall likewise be made to pay a hundred.
For approaching a non-human womb,
one incurs the first <s>sāhasa</s> penalty;
one incurs the middling fine
for approaching a buffalo.
One incurs a fine of one thousand
if a man approaches a cow;
thus indeed the penalties are doubled
for those who are observing a <s>vrata</s> (penance).
To one weary on the road and of equal status,
one should give way or offer shelter;
one who fails to give becomes a ram of <s>Yama</s>;
one who does not give directions or shelter likewise.
A <s>Vipra</s> (brahmin) who consorts with a <s>Śūdrā</s> woman
is regarded as lower than a <s>Śūdra</s>;
by the very act of approaching
a <s>Śūdrā</s> woman, he becomes fallen.
By union with a <s>Śūdrā</s> woman,
a <s>Dvija</s> (twice-born) who has offspring becomes identified with her;
the mother of that <s>Śūdra</s> child —
they declare the fall from caste.
Therefore, a <s>Śūdra</s> for the purpose of sacrifice,
or even for domestic rites, a <s>Dvija</s>,
sowing white seed in dark soil —
such a <s>Vipra</s> is regarded as one who has extinguished his sacred fire.
Having seen offspring from a <s>Śūdrā</s> woman,
they go to great calamity;
the people's wealth he should take by policy,
or himself, if not a <s>Dvija</s>.
Even of impure dogs,
the goat's tooth is auspicious;
a <s>Dvija</s> who goes to a <s>Śūdrā</s> — let him behold
the ancestors shall examine him.
Therefore, in <s>Śrāddha</s> rites, one must certainly
reject a <s>Vipra</s> who is the husband of a <s>Vṛṣalī</s>,
and rejecting even dogs,
a <s>Dvija</s> should feed <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.
Food touched by the husband of a <s>Vṛṣalī</s>,
or looked upon, or eaten, or mixed by him,
all such food becomes unfit to eat;
even cooked food, once so affected, is likewise.
Of those excluded from the row and inauspicious persons,
even a <s>Dvija</s> equal in the row,
should take only mature grain;
a husband of a <s>Vṛṣalī</s> is grouped among them.
A father touched by copper
and likewise by silver,
can be purified by the wise;
but if touched during a <s>Śrāddha</s>, it is destroyed.
A <s>Vipra</s> touched by a <s>Kṣatriya</s> woman,
and likewise by a <s>Vaiśya</s> woman,
attains purification through prescribed means;
but not one who has gone to a <s>Śūdrā</s> woman.
A king who is indifferent
toward the husband of a <s>Vṛṣalī</s> in his village,
that king becomes unworthy of receiving gifts;
the village itself likewise, for its own interests.
Of all <s>kaṇṭakas</s> (thorns, i.e., criminals),
the one who wields power is the violent offender;
therefore, for the violent offender, the king
should ordain the penalty of banishment.
One who commits a minor violent offense,
who over time becomes a habitual offender,
since indeed sin accumulates —
reflecting thus, one should punish him.
Thus from various classes the king
should uproot the <s>kaṇṭakas</s> (criminals);
<s>Dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>artha</s> (wealth), longevity,
fame, and the kingdom thereby increase.
Regarding the <s>kaṇṭakas</s> (criminals), what has been stated
by the first principle of justice,
the fourfold procedure is declared;
it succeeds through the proper path.
Family and other factors in a dispute,
in hearing, are established by authoritative tradition;
even in a corner, acquired through the <s>śāstras</s> (scriptures),
by a learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
